class.name: SettingsServer
class.brief_description: Base class of the settings servers: one domain of player settings (audio, video, language, game options, ...) that is loaded, applied and saved.

method.name: _apply
method.description: Called by [method apply] to push values that have no binding to the engine. [param settings] is the settings resource to apply (including session overrides), [param names] are the names of the values that changed and have no binding. Values with a binding are pushed by the binding and are not part of [param names].

method.name: _create_settings
method.description: Returns a new [Resource] whose stored properties (for example [code]@export[/code] variables) are the settings of this domain, with the default values of the class. Called once, the first time the settings are needed. Required. If it returns [code]null[/code], an error is printed and an empty [Resource] is used. After this call, the engine state is read into the resource ([method _read_from_engine] and the getters of the bindings), and the optional defaults from [code]settings/defaults/<domain>[/code] are applied. The result becomes [method get_default_settings]. Properties named [code]script[/code] or starting with [code]resource_[/code], [code]metadata/[/code] or [code]__[/code], and properties without storage usage, are not settings.

method.name: _get_apply_phase
method.description: Returns the [enum ApplyPhase] in which [SettingsServerManager] starts this server while the game starts. The default is [constant APPLY_PHASE_SERVERS]. [constant APPLY_PHASE_NONE] and values outside the range of [enum ApplyPhase] are clamped to the first or the last phase. [b]Note:[/b] A script domain listed in [member ProjectSettings.settings/startup/custom_servers] is created in [constant APPLY_PHASE_SCENE], the latest phase, and is started at once, whatever this method returns: scripts can't run before the [DisplayServer] exists. Only a domain written in C++ (an engine module or a GDExtension registered at the servers level) can start in [constant APPLY_PHASE_PRE_DISPLAY] or [constant APPLY_PHASE_SERVERS]. A domain registered after its phase (for example by an autoload) is started when it is registered.

method.name: _get_domain
method.description: Returns the name of the domain, for example [code]&"game"[/code]. Required. It is used as the file name ([code]user://settings/<domain>.ini[/code]) and as the key in [SettingsServerManager]. It must not change while the server is registered.

method.name: _get_format_version
method.description: Returns the version of the settings format of this domain. The default is [code]1[/code]. It is written to the file as [code]metadata/settings_version[/code]. Increase it when you rename or convert values, and convert the old data in [method _migrate].

method.name: _is_value_supported
method.description: Returns [code]false[/code] if the setting [param name] is not supported on the current platform or hardware, so that a menu can hide or disable it. The default is [code]true[/code]. [method is_value_supported] calls this and returns [code]false[/code] for names that are not settings of the domain.

method.name: _migrate
method.description: Called by [method load] when the file was written with a version lower than [method get_format_version]. [param data] is the content of the file in the layout of the JSON format (keys are the setting names). Return the data converted to the current version. Metadata keys ([code]$type[/code], [code]metadata/*[/code]) are not meant to be changed. Not called for files without [code]metadata/settings_version[/code] and not for CSV files. If the file has a higher version than the game, a warning is printed and the data is read as it is.

method.name: _read_from_engine
method.description: Called by [method read_from_engine] and while the defaults are captured. Write the current engine state of the values that have no binding into [param settings]. Values with a binding are read through the binding.

method.name: _validate_value
method.description: Called by [method set_value], [method set_session_override] and [method load] for every value, after the built-in checks (range hints are clamped, enum hints are rejected with an error and the old value is kept). Return the value to use, for example a corrected value. The default returns [param value] unchanged.

method.name: _value_applied
method.description: Called once per value after it reached the engine and the applied copy is updated, before [signal applied] is emitted. [param value] is the value the engine uses now (a session override wins over the stored value). It is called by [method apply] (also at startup after the file is loaded, and after [method reset_to_defaults] in [constant APPLY_MODE_IMMEDIATE]), by [method apply_with_confirmation], by [method cancel_confirmation] for the restored values, and when a session override is set or cleared. It is not called for pending changes in [constant APPLY_MODE_MANUAL], nor by [method confirm_changes] (the values reached the engine already). Values with [constant SETTING_FLAG_NO_ENGINE_TARGET] are included: they count as applied when [method apply] stores them. Emit the typed signals of your domain here, for example [code]volume_changed(volume)[/code], so the game does not compare value names. The built-in domains emit theirs from the C++ counterpart of this method, for example [code]bus_volume_changed[/code] of [AudioBusSettingsServer].

method.name: apply
method.description: Pushes all values that differ between the pending and the applied copy to the engine, makes the pending copy the applied one, emits [signal applied] and queues an autosave. Returns [constant OK] when there is nothing to apply. If one of the changed values has [constant SETTING_FLAG_CONFIRM] (and the server is not starting), [method apply_with_confirmation] is called instead and its result is returned. Values with [constant SETTING_FLAG_RESTART_REQUIRED] are listed in [method get_restart_required_names] and reported with [signal restart_required]. If a confirmation is pending ([method is_confirmation_pending]), it is kept first ([method confirm_changes]: [signal confirmation_finished] with [code]true[/code]): the player changed more settings while the confirmation dialog was open, so the pending values work. A later [method cancel_confirmation] only reverts the values of a new confirmation.

method.name: apply_with_confirmation
method.description: Applies the pending changes like [method apply], keeps a backup of the previous applied state and waits for [method confirm_changes]. If it is not called within [param timeout_sec] seconds, [method cancel_confirmation] restores the backup. A negative [param timeout_sec] uses [member ProjectSettings.settings/general/confirmation_timeout]. Emits [signal confirmation_requested]. The changes are not saved until they are confirmed. Returns [constant OK] when there is nothing to apply. If a confirmation is already pending, it is kept first ([method confirm_changes]), then the new confirmation starts with its own backup and timeout.

method.name: bind_setting_callbacks
method.description: Binds the setting [param name] to two callables: [param setter] is called with the new value to push it to the engine, [param getter] is called without arguments and returns the current engine value (used by [method read_from_engine] and for the defaults). [param getter] can be invalid if the engine state can't be read. Replaces an earlier binding of the same setting. Reports an error if [param setter] is not valid.

method.name: bind_setting_property
method.description: Binds the setting [param name] to the property [param property] of [param target]. The server keeps only the instance ID of [param target]; if the object is freed, a warning is printed when the value is pushed.

method.name: bind_setting_singleton_property
method.description: Binds the setting [param name] to the property [param property] of the engine singleton called [param singleton], for example [code]&"Engine"[/code] with [code]&"max_fps"[/code]. The singleton is looked up each time, so it only has to exist when the value is pushed; otherwise a warning is printed.

method.name: cancel_confirmation
method.description: Restores the state from before [method apply_with_confirmation], pushes the old values to the engine and emits [signal value_changed] and [signal applied] for them and [signal confirmation_finished] with [code]false[/code]. Does nothing if no confirmation is pending. Called automatically when the timeout ends.

method.name: clear_session_override
method.description: Removes the session override of the setting [param name] and pushes the applied value to the engine again. Does nothing if there is no override.

method.name: confirm_changes
method.description: Keeps the changes of [method apply_with_confirmation], queues an autosave and emits [signal confirmation_finished] with [code]true[/code]. Does nothing if no confirmation is pending.

method.name: get_applied_settings
method.description: Returns the settings resource with the values the engine uses now. Do not change it; use [method set_value].

method.name: get_applied_value
method.description: Returns the applied value of the setting [param name]. Reports an error and returns [code]null[/code] if the domain has no such setting.

method.name: get_apply_phase
method.description: Returns the phase in which [SettingsServerManager] starts this server, from [method _get_apply_phase]. The default is [constant APPLY_PHASE_SERVERS].

method.name: get_confirmation_time_left
method.description: Returns the seconds left until a pending confirmation is canceled, or [code]0.0[/code] if no confirmation is pending.

method.name: get_default_settings
method.description: Returns the settings resource with the default values (see the description of the class). Do not change it.

method.name: get_default_value
method.description: Returns the default value of the setting [param name]. Reports an error and returns [code]null[/code] if the domain has no such setting.

method.name: get_dirty_setting_names
method.description: Returns the names of the settings whose pending value differs from the applied value.

method.name: get_domain
method.description: Returns the name of the domain, from [method _get_domain].

method.name: get_format_version
method.description: Returns the version of the settings format, from [method _get_format_version]. The default is [code]1[/code].

method.name: get_restart_required_names
method.description: Returns the names of the settings with [constant SETTING_FLAG_RESTART_REQUIRED] whose applied value differs from the value the engine started with. Their new values take effect after a restart. A name is removed when its value is applied back to the value of the start (also by [method cancel_confirmation] or [method reset_to_defaults]), and the list is cleared when [SettingsServerManager] starts the server. Before the server is started, the defaults are the values of the start.

method.name: get_setting_flags
method.description: Returns the [enum SettingFlags] of the setting [param name]. Returns [constant SETTING_FLAG_NONE] for settings without flags.

method.name: get_setting_names
method.description: Returns the names of all settings of the domain: the stored properties of the settings resource.

method.name: get_settings
method.description: Returns the pending settings resource, with the values that [method set_value] changed. Do not change it directly; use [method set_value], so that validation, signals and [method apply] are not skipped.

method.name: get_value
method.description: Returns the pending value of the setting [param name]. In [constant APPLY_MODE_IMMEDIATE] this is also the applied value. Reports an error and returns [code]null[/code] if the domain has no such setting.

method.name: has_session_override
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the setting [param name] has a session override.

method.name: has_setting
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the domain has a setting called [param name].

method.name: has_unsaved_changes
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if values were applied since the last successful [method save] and the file is not up to date. Not set by changes that are only pending, and not by changes that wait for a confirmation.

method.name: is_confirmation_pending
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while [method apply_with_confirmation] waits for [method confirm_changes].

method.name: is_dirty
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if there are pending values that are not applied ([method get_dirty_setting_names] is not empty).

method.name: is_setting_bound
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the setting [param name] has a binding to the engine.

method.name: is_started
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if [SettingsServerManager] has started the server: the defaults are captured, the file is loaded and the values are applied.

method.name: is_value_supported
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the domain has a setting [param name] and [method _is_value_supported] does not report it as unsupported on this platform.

method.name: load
method.description: Reads the settings file into the pending copy: the defaults, with the values from the file on top. Values that are missing in the file keep their default. Values from the file are validated ([method _validate_value]) and old files are converted with [method _migrate]. Emits [signal settings_changed] with the values that changed and then [signal loaded]. Nothing is pushed to the engine; call [method apply] to use the values. Returns [constant ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND] if there is no file yet; the defaults are used and no warning is printed. Returns an error code, prints a warning, emits [signal load_failed] and uses the defaults if the file can't be read or is not valid; the file is not overwritten until the next [method save].

method.name: read_from_engine
method.description: Reads the current engine state of the bound values (and [method _read_from_engine]) into the pending copy and makes it the applied copy. Use it after the engine changed a value by other means, for example the window was resized by the player. Emits [signal settings_changed] with the values that changed, then [signal read_from_engine_finished]. Values without a getter keep their pending value.

method.name: reset_to_defaults
method.description: Sets all pending values to the defaults, clears the session overrides of the changed values and emits [signal value_changed] for each changed value, [signal settings_changed] once and [signal reset]. In [constant APPLY_MODE_IMMEDIATE] the defaults are applied at once.

method.name: reset_value
method.description: Sets the setting [param name] to its default value, like [method set_value]. Reports an error if the domain has no such setting.

method.name: revert
method.description: Drops all pending changes: the pending copy is set to the applied copy. Emits [signal value_changed] for each changed value and [signal settings_changed] once.

method.name: save
method.description: Writes the applied state to the settings file and creates the folder if needed. While a confirmation is pending, the state from before the confirmation is written. With [member ProjectSettings.settings/general/only_changed_values], only values that differ from the defaults are written (INI and JSON). Values are compared by their stored properties, like [method is_dirty]: the list of a [ListSettingsServer] is not written while its entries have the values of the default entries, even though they are other resources. Emits [signal saved]. Returns an error code, prints an error and emits [signal save_failed] if the file can't be written (also when the text can't be built, the folder can't be created or the path is read-only, such as [code]res://[/code] in an exported game). [b]Note:[/b] Pending values that are not applied are not saved. A save that was queued by autosave is cleared.

method.name: set_session_override
method.description: Pushes [param value] for the setting [param name] to the engine without changing the stored value. The override is validated, never saved, and does not change [method get_value]. It stays until [method clear_session_override], [method set_value] for the same setting, or [method reset_to_defaults].

method.name: set_setting_flags
method.description: Sets the [enum SettingFlags] of the setting [param name]. The setting does not need a binding.

method.name: set_value
method.description: Changes the pending value of the setting [param name]. The value is validated first (a [float] is snapped to the step of its range hint or to [code]0.001[/code] with [method snap_float], range hints are clamped, invalid enum values are rejected with an error, then [method _validate_value] is called and a [float] it returns is snapped again). A session override of the setting is removed. If the value changed, [signal value_changed] and [signal settings_changed] are emitted and, in [constant APPLY_MODE_IMMEDIATE], [method apply] is called. Reports an error if the domain has no such setting.

method.name: snap_float
method.description: Returns [param value] with at most three decimals, as the settings servers store every [float] setting: snapped to [param step] relative to [param offset] (a step below [code]0.001[/code] counts as [code]0.001[/code]), then to [code]0.001[/code]. [code]-0.0[/code] becomes [code]0.0[/code]; infinite and NaN values are returned unchanged. The settings servers use the step and the minimum of the property's range hint ([code]"-80,24,0.1"[/code] snaps to [code]0.1[/code]); a [float] without a range hint or with a smaller step is snapped to [code]0.001[/code]. This applies to [method set_value], session overrides, loaded files, defaults, values read from the engine and the float fields of list entries ([ListSettingsServer]). [method get_value], [method get_applied_value], [method get_default_value] and [signal value_changed] return the snapped value, also for a setting stored as a 32-bit float ([code]0.2[/code], not [code]0.20000000298023224[/code]). [codeblocks] [gdscript] print(SettingsServer.snap_float(0.30000000000000004)) # 0.3 print(SettingsServer.snap_float(-6.0206, 0.1)) # -6.0 print(SettingsServer.snap_float(-0.0000014)) # 0.0 [/gdscript] [csharp] GD.Print(SettingsServer.SnapFloat(0.30000000000000004)); // 0.3 GD.Print(SettingsServer.SnapFloat(-6.0206, 0.1)); // -6 GD.Print(SettingsServer.SnapFloat(-0.0000014)); // 0 [/csharp] [/codeblocks]

method.name: unbind_setting
method.description: Removes the binding of the setting [param name]. The flags of the setting are removed with it.

members.member: When changed values are applied: at once or when [method apply] is called.

The path of the settings file. The getter returns the path in use, which is the first of: - the path set with the setter at runtime; - [code]<folder>/<file_name>.<extension of the format>[/code] from the project settings, for example [code]user://settings/audio.ini[/code] (the default) or [code]user://settings/profiles/audio.json[/code]. The folder is [member ProjectSettings.settings/general/folder] (see [method SettingsServerManager.get_storage_folder]). The file name is [code]settings/<domain>/file_name[/code] without extension, by default the domain name; it may contain a relative subfolder, which [method save] creates. An absolute path, a path with [code]..[/code] or an empty folder name is rejected with an error and the domain name is used. The format is [member ProjectSettings.settings/general/default_format] (see [method SettingsServerManager.get_storage_format]), or [code]settings/<domain>/format[/code] if [code]settings/<domain>/override_format[/code] is [code]true[/code]. [SettingsServerManager] defines the three settings of the domain group when the domain registers, so the engine domains show them in [b]Project Settings > Settings[/b] (advanced settings). Script domains from [member ProjectSettings.settings/startup/custom_servers] define them when the game runs; add them by hand in the editor with these names. For a path set at runtime, the format is taken from the extension of the path ([method ResourceTextSerializer.get_format_from_extension]): [code].json[/code], [code].ini[/code], [code].csv[/code] (only [ListSettingsServer]), [code].xml[/code], [code].toml[/code], [code].yaml[/code] or [code].yml[/code]. An unknown extension, or a format whose module is not in the build, prints an error once that names the domain and the path; the file is then read and written in the format of [member ProjectSettings.settings/general/default_format] (or of its domain group [code]settings/<domain>/[/code]). [b]Note:[/b] Use a [code]user://[/code] path. [code]res://[/code] is read-only in exported games, and on the Web only [code]user://[/code] is writable (kept in IndexedDB); absolute paths work on desktop platforms only.

signal.name: applied
signal.description: Emitted after values were pushed to the engine, with the names of the values. Also emitted when a pending confirmation is canceled and the old values are restored.

signal.name: confirmation_finished
signal.description: Emitted when a confirmation ends. [param kept] is [code]true[/code] after [method confirm_changes] and [code]false[/code] after [method cancel_confirmation] or when the time is over.

signal.name: confirmation_requested
signal.description: Emitted when [method apply_with_confirmation] starts waiting. Show a dialog with a countdown ([method get_confirmation_time_left]) and call [method confirm_changes] or [method cancel_confirmation].

signal.name: load_failed
signal.description: Emitted by [method load] when the file at [param path] exists but can't be read or is not valid, or there is no path; [param error] is the error that [method load] returns. The defaults are used; [signal loaded] follows. Not emitted when there is no file yet (the normal first start).

signal.name: loaded
signal.description: Emitted when [method load] has finished, also if there was no file or the file was not valid (then after [signal load_failed]).

signal.name: reset
signal.description: Emitted by [method reset_to_defaults], after [signal value_changed] for the changed values.

signal.name: restart_required
signal.description: Emitted when the list of [method get_restart_required_names] changes: a value with [constant SETTING_FLAG_RESTART_REQUIRED] was applied and differs from the value the engine started with, or was applied back to it. [param names] is the whole list after the change; an empty list means that no restart is needed any more. Not emitted while the server starts.

signal.name: save_failed
signal.description: Emitted by [method save] (also a save queued by autosave) when the file at [param path] can't be written; [param error] is the error that [method save] returns. The file keeps its old content and [method has_unsaved_changes] stays [code]true[/code]. Show a message, or try another path with [member file_path].

signal.name: saved
signal.description: Emitted when [method save] has written the file.

signal.name: settings_changed
signal.description: Emitted once after an operation that changed pending values, with the names of all changed values: [method set_value] (and [method reset_value]), [method revert], [method reset_to_defaults], [method load], [method read_from_engine], and a confirmation that was canceled or timed out. Not emitted when nothing changed. Connect a whole options menu to this signal instead of [signal value_changed], which is emitted per value and not by [method load] and [method read_from_engine]. In [constant APPLY_MODE_IMMEDIATE] it comes before [signal applied].

signal.name: value_changed
signal.description: Emitted when the pending value of a setting changed, with the new value: by [method set_value], [method reset_value], [method revert], [method reset_to_defaults] and a canceled confirmation. In [constant APPLY_MODE_MANUAL] this is before the value is applied. [method load] and [method read_from_engine] emit only [signal settings_changed].

constants.constant: [method set_value] and the other changes are applied at once.
Changes stay pending until [method apply] is called, and can be dropped with [method revert].
No phase: [SettingsServerManager] has not started any phase yet (see [method SettingsServerManager.get_startup_phase]).

Started right after the servers and modules are registered, before the [DisplayServer] is created. Use it for values that the window needs at creation, such as the window mode or the rendering driver.
Started after all servers and the script languages are initialized and the default bus layout is loaded. This is the default phase.

Started after the [SceneTree] and the root window exist, before the main scene is loaded and before the [code]_ready()[/code] of the autoloads. Script domains from [member ProjectSettings.settings/startup/custom_servers] are started in this phase.
Represents the size of the [enum ApplyPhase] enum.

The per-viewport values of a graphics settings server ([RenderQualitySettingsServer], [ShadowSettingsServer], [TextureSettingsServer]) go to the root viewport and to the viewports added with the server's [code]add_viewport()[/code] only.
The per-viewport values also go to every [Viewport] in the server's group ([code]get_viewport_group()[/code]), also when it enters the tree later. The default.
The per-viewport values also go to every viewport in [ViewportServer] ([SubViewport]s, embedded and native [Window]s), also when it enters the tree later.
The engine reads the value only at startup. After it was applied, the setting is listed in [method get_restart_required_names] and [signal restart_required] is emitted.
Changes of the value go through [method apply_with_confirmation], also in [constant APPLY_MODE_IMMEDIATE]. Use it for values that can make the game unusable, such as the video mode.
The value is only stored for the game and never pushed to the engine, even if a binding exists.
